## Key terms

{{< glossary digital-media digitization raster-image vector-graphics multimedia elemental-tetrad mechanics aesthetics player-experience asset production-pipeline pre-production >}}

## 1.1 What digital media are

**Digital media** are text, images, audio, video, animation and interactive
content encoded as numbers. Sound and light are continuous; **digitization**
turns them into numbers by **sampling** (measuring at regular intervals) and
**quantization** (rounding each measurement to fixed levels). Uncompressed
media are huge — one second of CD audio is about 176 KB, one full-HD frame
about 6.2 MB — so games use compressed formats. A **raster** image is a grid
of pixels; **vector graphics** store shapes and scale without loss.

![Digitizing a sound wave: sampling and quantization.](images/sampling.png){width=86%}

![Raster (pixels) and vector (shapes) versions of one icon.](images/raster-vector.png){width=72%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Media as numbers"}
Choose the right term or value.

::: {.match extra="raster|6.2 MB"}
Measuring a sound wave at regular intervals.
:   sampling

Rounding each measurement to one of a fixed set of levels.
:   quantization

The number of samples per second used by audio CDs.
:   44 100

The size of one second of uncompressed CD stereo audio.
:   about 176 KB

The image type that stays sharp at any size.
:   vector graphics

A work that combines several types of media.
:   multimedia
:::
:::

## 1.2 Properties of digital media

Because they are numbers, digital media are **computable** (code changes
colours and volumes at runtime), **modular** (levels are assembled from
reusable assets), open to **automation** (procedural levels), **variable**
(one work in many versions, such as adaptive music or translations) and
**transcoded** between computer data and human culture. Above all, game media
are **interactive**: they must be designed as a set of possibilities — a sound
may play once or a hundred times.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Which property?"}
Choose the property of digital media that each example shows.

::: {.match extra="numerical representation"}
A level is built from the same 40 tiles used again and again.
:   modularity

The music adds drums and strings when an enemy comes near.
:   variability

A program generates a new dungeon for every game.
:   automation

The same sound may play once or a hundred times, depending on the player.
:   interactivity
:::
:::

## 1.3 The game as a composite medium

Schell's **elemental tetrad** describes a game as **mechanics** (rules and
actions), **story** (events), **aesthetics** (how it looks, sounds and feels)
and **technology** (device, engine). No element is more important than the
others. The goal of all four is the **player experience**; media succeed only
when they strengthen it.

![The elemental tetrad.](images/tetrad.png)
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![Lantern Keeper: all four elements create one experience.](images/lantern-keeper.png)
:::
::::

{{< sim file="sims/juice-it.html" poster="sims/juice-it.png" title="Juice It: same mechanics, different media" kind="game" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Watch out!"}
Aesthetics are not only graphics. Music, sound, vibration and the rhythm of
animation are aesthetics too.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The tetrad of Lantern Keeper"}
Lantern Keeper: a lantern spirit floats through a dark forest to relight a
village before sunrise. Which element of the tetrad is each sentence about?

::: {.match}
Tap to float upward; fireflies make the light grow.
:   mechanics

The spirit must relight the lanterns before sunrise.
:   story

Warm light in a cold blue forest; soft piano music.
:   aesthetics

A cheap light shader keeps 60 fps on old phones.
:   technology

What all four elements together are designed to produce.
:   the player experience
:::
:::

## 1.4 The creative production pipeline

Media pass through **pre-production** (concept, premise, script, storyboard,
style guide, schedule), **production** (making the **assets**: art, models,
music, voices, sound effects, video), **post-production** (editing, mixing,
colour, compression, export), then integration and testing — which often send
work back. Every asset has an owner at every stage (intellectual property,
weeks 13–14).

![The production pipeline.](images/pipeline.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Which stage?"}
Choose the stage of the pipeline. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match}
Writing the script and drawing the storyboard.
:   pre-production

Recording the voices of the characters.
:   production

Mixing the music and exporting compressed files.
:   post-production

A tester reports that a sound is too loud next to the music.
:   integration and testing

Composing the music.
:   production
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Lantern Keeper's media plan {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

The *Lantern Keeper* team must plan its media. The game needs a 2-minute
looping music track, a firefly chime with three variations, a vector logo for
the store page and a 30-second trailer. The music has three layers that are
added as danger grows. The team works in the order of the pipeline.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Planning the media (harder)"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="raster|pre-production"}
The size of the music if it were stored as uncompressed CD stereo audio (176 KB per second).
:   about 21 MB

The property of digital media shown by the three music layers.
:   variability

Why the chime has three variations instead of one.
:   so it does not repeat identically

The image type for the logo, used on a tiny icon and on a large banner.
:   vector

The stage in which the trailer is edited and exported.
:   post-production
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Digital media = content encoded as numbers; digitization = sampling + quantization.
- Uncompressed media are huge, so games use compressed formats.
- Raster = pixels; vector = shapes that scale.
- Digital media are computable, modular, automatable, variable, transcoded — and interactive.
- Tetrad: mechanics, story, aesthetics, technology → player experience.
- Pipeline: pre-production → production → post-production → integration and testing.
